watch.title: Keep the session on your wrist.
watch.body: We’re developing Watch starts, delivered results and running dynamics. Your paired iPhone connects the Watch to the timing session.
steps: Pair the Watch to the host/start iPhone for Watch starts.
Use other phones for your finish and optional splits.
Review the time, then explore available movement metrics.
watch.requirement: Development preview · Not in the public app yet

gates.title: One session. Every split.
gates.body: Put phones at the start and finish. Add another at a split to see how your speed changes across the run.
steps: Measure the course and position each phone.
Create or join the same session and wait for every gate to be ready.
Run through. Review the time and crossing photos together.

solo.title: Just you. One phone.
solo.body: Set one camera at a line you pass repeatedly. The first crossing starts the session; each later crossing records a lap and photo.
steps: Fix the phone beside a clearly marked line.
Choose Solo Laps and check the camera view.
Cross the same line for each lap or return.
solo.requirement: 1 phone · Repeated crossings of the same line

agility.title: One camera. The whole drill.
agility.body: Landscape timing in development for standing and flying sprints, 5-10-5 and out-and-back drills. Keep the measured course in view.
steps: For 5-10-5, mark three lines 5 yards apart.
Start at centre, touch both outside lines, return to centre.
The first centre return is a split. Review both touches on video.
agility.requirement: Development preview · Tripod and video turn review

starts.title: Five ways to get going.
starts.description: Choose the timing anchor that matches your test. Compare results recorded with the same start method.

items.title: Flying start
items.body: Build speed before the first gate. Crossing the start line begins the timed zone.

items.title: Touch release
items.body: Hold the start phone’s screen. Lifting your finger starts the timer.

items.title: Countdown
items.body: A countdown leads into an audible signal. Timing begins on the cue and includes your response.

items.title: Voice command
items.body: Follow spoken start commands. The timer begins on GO.

items.title: In-frame start
items.body: Stand at the start phone’s front-camera gate. Cross the on-screen line to begin.

founder.title: Built by an athlete who uses it.

founder.imageAlt: Sondre Guttormsen competing in pole vault

items.question: Can I use just one phone?
items.answer: Yes. Solo Laps records repeated crossings at one camera line. Separate start and finish positions use connected phones. The landscape one-camera sprint and agility modes are still in development.

items.question: Do I need Wi-Fi or internet?
items.answer: Supported nearby connections can time locally without internet. Wi-Fi Aware requires compatible hardware and software; Bluetooth is another supported connection option. Cloud features need connectivity.

items.question: How accurate is it?
items.answer: Results depend on camera frame rate, lighting, positioning, the start method and clock synchronization. The number of decimal places is not an accuracy guarantee. Use a stable setup and review the crossing photos. TrackSpeed is for training, not official competition timing.

items.question: Does it work with Apple Watch or Android?
items.answer: The public experience described here is for iPhone and iPad. Watch features and landscape agility modes are in development. Android is also being developed; this site does not promise feature parity across platforms.

items.question: What does TrackSpeed cost?
items.answer: The app is free to download with in-app purchases. Check the app for the plans, price, trial eligibility and features available in your region.
